purpose: S012 — Language and Pronunciation (언어와 발음의 경계)
previous: S011 = 보컬 질감/전달. S012 = 보컬 축의 나머지 절반 — 언어, 발음, 장르 편향
theme: 한국어→K-Pop 장르 편향 존재, 발음/딕션 지시(17회)는 미지 영역 — 언어가 장르를 결정하는가?
method: Suno Custom 모드 생성 → 풀 길이 재업로드 → SP+가사 라운드트립

test_axes: 코드 스위칭(한 곡 안에서 언어 전환)이 가능한가

test_prompts.title: Language Bias Test
test_prompts.concept: 4개 언어 편향 비교 — 동일한 SP + 다른 언어 가사. 한국어→K-Pop 편향이 실제 존재하는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: Korean(한국어 가사 시 K-Pop 편향 보고), English(기본), Japanese(관측 미비), Spanish(관측 미비)
test_prompts.sp: Indie folk song with acoustic guitar fingerpicking, upright bass, light brushed drums, and harmonica. Warm, intimate, singer-songwriter style. Simple chord progression in G major. Gentle male vocal. The arrangement, instrumentation, and style must remain exactly the same regardless of what language the lyrics are in. This is an English-language version. The song should sound like American indie folk, not K-pop, not J-pop, not Latin pop. 95 BPM in G major. 4/4 time. Acoustic home recording.

The garden needs attention and the fence needs paint
The dog is getting older and my patience wearing thin

Something in the morning says the fog is going to lift

[Chorus]
The road keeps going
And the river keeps flowing

[Outro]
(humming the melody)
Mmm mmm mmm...

test_prompts.title: Accent Direction
test_prompts.concept: 억양/액센트 지시 — SP에서 특정 발음 스타일(Southern American, British, Irish)을 요구했을 때 반영되는가?
test_prompts.sp: Country folk song sung with a thick Southern American accent. The vocalist should drawl every vowel, drop the g from every -ing ending, and pronounce words the way they sound in rural Tennessee. The word fire becomes fahr. The word going becomes goin. The word night becomes naht. The accent should be unmistakable and consistent throughout — not a caricature but an authentic deep Southern singing voice, the kind heard in traditional Appalachian folk music. Acoustic guitar, banjo, fiddle, upright bass. 100 BPM in D major. 3/4 time. Porch recording.

test_prompts.title: Diction Clarity
test_prompts.concept: 딕션(발음 선명도) 지시 — 극도로 명확한 발음 vs 극도로 불명확한 발음. SP 지시에 반응하는가?
test_prompts.sp: Pop song with two contrasting vocal sections testing diction control. Section A requires crystal clear diction — every consonant is crisp and precise, every vowel is pure, every word is perfectly enunciated as if the singer is a trained broadcaster. Every single syllable must be intelligible on first listen with no ambiguity. Section B requires extremely unclear diction — the vocals are mumbled, slurred, vowels blending into each other, consonants swallowed, words running together, the kind of singing where you cannot make out the lyrics without a lyric sheet. The contrast between the two sections should be dramatic. Same melody, same key, same accompaniment. Piano and light drums. 100 BPM in C major. 4/4 time.

test_prompts.title: Code Switching
test_prompts.concept: 코드 스위칭 — 한 곡 안에서 영어↔한국어 전환. 언어 전환 시 장르/음악 스타일이 변하는가?
test_prompts.sp: Pop song that switches between English and Korean lyrics within the same musical arrangement. The instrumentation and production style must remain constant throughout — synth pop with electronic beats, synthesizer pads, and modern production. When the lyrics switch from English to Korean, the music should NOT change style. The genre should remain synth pop regardless of language. The verse is in English, the chorus is in Korean, the bridge switches between both languages line by line. Male vocal. 118 BPM in A minor. 4/4 time. Modern pop production.

test_prompts.title: Syllable Density
test_prompts.concept: 음절 밀도 — 같은 멜로디에 음절이 빽빽한 가사 vs 음절이 희박한 가사. 가사 밀도가 음악에 미치는 영향
test_prompts.sp: Hip-hop and ballad hybrid testing syllable density contrast. Section A is a rapid-fire rap verse with maximum syllable density — as many syllables as possible crammed into each bar, tongue-twister speed, every beat subdivided into multiple syllables, the words tumbling over each other in a stream. Section B is an open ballad verse with minimum syllable density — one or two words per bar, long held notes, vast spaces between words, the opposite of rap's compression. Both sections use the same 90 BPM tempo and the same chord progression in D minor. The only difference is how many syllables occupy each bar. Trap beat with 808 bass for Section A, piano ballad for Section B. 90 BPM in D minor. 4/4 time.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Section A — maximum syllable density, rap]
(rapid-fire, as many syllables as possible per beat)

[Section A continued]
(still rapid-fire)
Never stopping never pausing never breathing never letting any empty space survive between the syllables because density is gravity and gravity is power and the words are planets orbiting the beat at the speed of thought

[Section B — minimum syllable density, ballad]
(one or two words per bar, long held notes)
Silence...

Is...

A language...

Too...

[Section B continued]
(vast spaces between words)
One...

Word...

Is...

Enough...

[Final — density increasing from minimum to maximum]
(starting sparse, ending dense)
One...
One word...
One word is all...
One word is all I need to say and every syllable that follows is another layer building on the first until the words are everywhere

test_prompts.title: Phoneme-Level Direction
test_prompts.concept: 음소 단위 발음 지시 — SP에서 특정 모음/자음의 처리 방식을 지정. 가장 세밀한 수준의 보컬 제어 시도
test_prompts.corpus_reference: pronunciation(0회), vowel(0회), consonant(0회), phoneme(0회) — 완전 데드존
test_prompts.sp: Art pop song with specific phoneme-level vocal instructions. The vocalist must elongate all open vowels — ah, oh, ee — holding them twice as long as normal, stretching each vowel sound into a sustained tone. Consonants should be percussive and sharp — every p, t, k should pop like a drum hit. The sibilant sounds — s, sh, z — should be exaggerated and drawn out like white noise. The letter r should be rolled with a trill on the tongue. The letter l should be dark and rounded. These phoneme-level instructions should create a vocal performance where every sound in the language is treated as a musical element with its own character. Art pop production with synths and programmed drums. 105 BPM in B minor. 4/4 time.
